recipes.name: Award-Winning Peaches and Cream Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package cook-and-serve vanilla pudding (not instant)
1 (29 ounce) can sliced peaches in heavy syrup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 10-inch deep-dish pie plate.
Whisk flour, pudding mix, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl until evenly combined; add milk, butter, and egg.
Beat crust mixture with an electric mixer for 2 minutes; transfer to the prepared pie plate.
Combine 1 tablespoon sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Beat cream cheese in separate bowl with an electric mixer until fluffy; add ½ cup sugar and reserved syrup and beat for 2 minutes.
Arrange sliced peaches over crust mixture.
Spoon cream cheese mixture over peaches to within 1 inch of pie plate edge; sprinkle cinnamon sugar over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 30 to 35 minutes.
Set aside on the counter for 20 minutes, then chill in the refrigerator before serving for at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Award-Winning Peaches and Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: This award-winning peaches and cream pie recipe has pudding mix in the crust, a layer of canned peaches, and another layer of sweetened cream cheese.

video.description: Your new year-round dessert will be widely celebrated and achieve top honors in the hearts of dessert lovers everywhere with its luscious combination of sliced canned peaches blended with sugar, cream cheese and peach syrup and spread over a crust of flour, salt, baking powder, vanilla pudding mix, butter egg and milk. Shake on some cinnamon sugar, bake until set, then chill completely before serving big slabs all around in exchange for big smiles.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely great dessert. I have made this four times and am ALWAYS asked for the recipe. Though on a side note, I always use 1.5 times the amount of peaches the recipe calls for. It's pretty darn fabulous. Definitely a keeper!!!

This was fabulous! I call it my second best find so far on this site, with the first one being the recipe for "Clone of a Cinnabon". I followed a previous reviewer's suggestion and doubled the recipe and baked it in a glass 9 x 13 pan. I then chilled it over night and brought it to work. Everyone loved it! I also would agree that it's not really a pie, but more like a peaches and cream dessert. I didn't find it too sweet at all and I like that it calls for canned peaches, so I can make it any time of year. Will definately make this again.

I like this okay with the peach, as written, but my friend and I decided we'd prefer lemon so I set out to make some changes; I have made the lemon variation at least a half dozen times since. Everyone loves it! I've made it in a deep dish pie plate, a square cake pan, and a large springform pan (greased and bottom lined with parchment paper so it can be slid off onto a pretty platter for serving). When making the lemon variation, I leave all the cinnamon off (from both the peach filling and the topping). Instead of the peach slices, I use a jar of lemon curd. And, in place of the peach juice in the cream cheese, I use Sicilian Limoncello liqueur. After it cools, I like to dust it with powdered sugar and garnish with a thin lemon slice.

We've made this pie 3 times in the past two weeks!!! A total hit!!! The first time we made everything according to the recipe. Then we decided, that we needed to add a tbsp of sugar or honey to the batter. It just didn't taste right without. That could be, because we live in Germany, and here there is no pre-added sugar in instant pudding packages. We preferred the flavor with honey. Then we decided to add a Tbsp. of cornstarch to the cream cheese mixture. If you are pressed for time, you get the firmness with out the hours of cooling and it is still creamy. The third time, we mixed peaches and mandarins. That was was a great combination. We'd like to try mango next time. Perhaps pureed mango over the peach slices? I'd upload a picture, but this pie just vaporizes to quickly :-))))

Great recipe! I made it twice for the potluck at work and received a lot of compliments! Second time I replaced canned peaches with fresh (pealled) and like that way much better. I slightly sauteed peaches with 1 Tbsp of peach liqueur and some sugar. I think I will keep this changes.

I made this Gluten Free since I can't have gluten due to an allergy and lower carb. I substituted an ancient grain gluten free flour mix for the flour. Instead of the pudding I used 2 eggs, 1/4 cup sugar substitute, 1 Tablespoon vanilla, 2 Tablespoons sour cream and 1/2 cup heavy cream instead of the milk. I used fresh peaches and blueberries and 1/4 cup sugar substitute for the 1/2 cup white sugar in the cream cheese. I like my desserts not as sweet as most people. I baked it in my deep dish baker from Pampered Chef and it was the perfect size. I can't say if it is as good as the original since I convert it to gluten free, but it turned out delicious. Thanks so much for the recipe and inspiration. I will be making this again and trying different fruits.
I just put in oven I didn't have deep dish so i used two pie plates and divided it in two. I used fresh peaches can't wait!!

I have been making this recipe for years. It's always a hit and is often requested. The only change I make is using French Vanilla rather than plain vanilla pudding. I prefer to serve it fresh from the oven or room temperature. Great with peach or vanilla ice cream. One year I did have to double the ingredients and use a 9x12 baking pan for a larger crowd.
I've made this for years. My family loves it. But I use the instant pudding instead of the cook and serve. It's delicious.
Fabulous! The one thing I did differently was use fresh peaches
Made the recipe using 4 fresh peaches and baked in a springform pan. Absolutely delicious! Will definitely make again.
I replace flour with GF 1:1 flour to make gluten free Andy family LOVES it.

Because i had no pudding mix i used Birds Original Custard Powder( added some vanilla &powdered sugar, cause custard powder isnt very sweet.) used fresh peaches. Smells great, hope my improvising works. Funny thing im not adventurous type but with cooking/ baking im always experimenting. Had epic fails, but more fantastic results .
It was delicious!
Sooo easy! Delicious! And a surprise when one expects a normal pie crust, but it's not ;)

My family and guests loved this pie. It is so delicious. I double the cinnamon on accident, but it was a very happy mistake. I need to figure out how to do this same pie with pumpkin for the holidays.
So easy and my husband who doesn’t like fruit, liked it and said I can make this anytime
I loved this and so did everyone else! The only change I made was to add some almond extract. Perfection 😀 I did double the recipe and bake in a 9x13 pan.
I made this for Easter and none of us liked it! It had nothing to offer. Would never make again! I threw most of it away. :(
I used to make this for my dad. He loved. I’m glad to have found the recipe again.
